thread:
maya: quick heads-up — CI eval job #237 started failing after the quantization branch landed. Workers stall and backlog spikes.

samir: saw it, reproducing locally. logs show worker loop hitting empty assignment repeatedly, queue depth grows to ~1k.

devon: can you paste the stack snippet? I pulled one:
```
2026-11-03 09:12:45,321 EvalRunner ERROR assign_shard() -> None
... EvalRunner loop: sleep(0.5)
QueueDepth=1023
```

liam: looks like the new split-allocator returns an empty assignment when variant=quant-small; small edge-case. Repro with:
`python tests/splitter_test.py --seed 42 --shards 16 --variant quant-small`

maya: ugh. that explains it. can we gate the allocator or fallback to full-range when assignment empty?

samir: yes — propose adding guard `if not assignment: assignment = [0..N-1]` and log a metric. I'll open a quick PR and push a canary job.

devon: PR 3892 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/3892 — adds guard + unit test. CI will run the new small-shard canary.

eval-bot: test-runner: eval-job-237 (canary) queued

maya: also let's add a short CI job in `eval-ci.yml` to run splitter_test with quant flags to catch this next time. example config:
```
- name: splitter-canary
  run: python tests/splitter_test.py --shards 4 --variant quant-small
  timeout-minutes: 10
```

samir: agreed. adding to canary matrix now. once green we'll merge and roll to staging.

ci-bot: Deployment to staging triggered by PR 3892 :rocket:

maya: :thumbsup: thanks team — keeping an eye on backlog metrics, will alert if queue > 500.
